post_text:
Sessions were fast.

Then the threads froze.

I was the lead architect for the new session service. We chose Redis, configuring a massive connection pool. I felt confident we had engineered away resource contention.

Black Friday traffic hit 4x peak projections. 📈

Latency immediately spiked to five seconds. The application servers weren't crashing, but they were completely unresponsive. Users saw 504 Gateway Timeouts. 💀

The Redis server CPU was idle. Memory was stable. The bottleneck wasn't the database; it was the application waiting for the database.

I thought the pool size was the only constraint. It never occurred to me that the application threads were holding connections hostage for too long.

We were using synchronous blocking I/O for every session lookup. A slow operation, multiplied by thousands of concurrent requests, instantly starved the pool. Every worker thread waited on network I/O, not CPU. We lost 15 minutes of peak revenue. ⏳

The immediate fix was switching the client library to non-blocking asynchronous calls.

The Moral 👇

The synchronous lease time of a pooled connection defines the ceiling of concurrent throughput.
